claim: India's nutraceutical market was valued at $4 billion in 2020 and projected to reach $18 billion by 2025, reflecting massive post-COVID growth in consumer demand for dietary supplements.
stance_target: Indian supplement market context for Briyo brand
quoted_support: India's nutraceutical market is booming, with projections suggesting it will reach $18 billion by 2025, up from just $4 billion in 2020.

claim: FSSAI's foundational nutraceutical regulation — FSS (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, etc.) Regulations 2016 — covers eight product categories including health supplements, functional foods, specialty foods containing botanicals, probiotics, prebiotics, and novel foods.
stance_target: Vitamin D3 supplements like Briyo fall under the FSSAI 2016 Regulations as health supplements
quoted_support: The Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food, and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016 established the foundational framework for nutraceutical regulation in India.

claim: A 2024 inter-ministerial committee recommended that high-potency nutraceuticals with pharmaceutical-grade excipients be shifted from FSSAI oversight to CDSCO, the drug regulator, while simple vitamins/minerals would remain under FSSAI.
stance_target: Potential future regulatory change that could affect high-dose Vitamin D3 products in India
scope_conditions: India, proposed regulatory reform from November 2024 committee recommendations
quoted_support: Simple supplements would remain under FSSAI's jurisdiction, while high-potency products with specific dosages and pharmaceutical-grade excipients would potentially fall under CDSCO regulation.

claim: Absence of strict pre-market approval for nutraceuticals in India has allowed misleading health claims to proliferate, as enforcement of FSS (Claims and Advertisements) Regulations 2018 remains challenging.
stance_target: FSSAI approval does not guarantee a product's health claims have been rigorously vetted
quoted_support: The absence of strict pre-market approval processes has allowed misleading health claims to flourish in the nutraceutical market. Many manufacturers make exaggerated or unsubstantiated claims about disease prevention, treatment, or cure.

claim: FSSAI issued interim directions in August 2024 to re-operationalize certain provisions of the proposed 2022 nutraceutical regulations while comprehensive reform is still pending.
stance_target: Current FSSAI regulatory status for nutraceuticals in India (as of 2024-2025)
quoted_support: FSSAI issued interim directions in August 2024 to re-operationalize certain provisions of the proposed 2022 regulations. This pragmatic approach allows businesses to continue operating under established guidelines while the inter-ministerial committee completes its review.
